issues.detail: The skill does not explicitly cover error handling or edge cases in the instructions, leaving potential gaps for users encountering failures.
The skill contains extensive explanatory text that may be considered padded, reducing overall conciseness.
The skill is vendor-locked to Liveblocks and specific to React/Next.js, limiting cross-platform applicability.

scenarios.name: setup-liveblocks-provider
scenarios.rationale: Response A includes all required elements (LiveblocksProvider with authEndpoint and throttle, RoomProvider with id, initialPresence, initialStorage using LiveList, and ClientSideSuspense with fallback), whereas Response B omits throttle, initialPresence, initialStorage, LiveList, and ClientSideSuspense.

scenarios.name: live-cursors-component
scenarios.rationale: Response B satisfies all rubric requirements, while Response A does not use the required hooks.

scenarios.name: liveblocks-auth-endpoint
scenarios.rationale: Response B fully satisfies the rubric by importing Liveblocks, creating an instance, preparing a session with userInfo, granting FULL_ACCESS, authorizing, and returning the token, whereas Response A omits these key steps.
